questions.question: In a certain code language, "PUNISHED" is written as "288" and "TAILOR" is written as "225". How is "RELEASED" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

P (16) + U (21) + N (14) + I (9) + S (19) + H (8) + E (5) + D (4) = 96 × 3 = 288

T (20) + A (1) + I (9) + L (12) + O (15) + R (18) = 75 × 3 = 225

Same pattern will be followed to answer the question:

R (18) + E (5) + L (12) + E (5) + A (1) + S (19) + E (5) + D (4) =** 69 × 3 = 207**

Hence, answer is 207.

questions.question: Ratio of present ages of P and Q is 9 : 4. The difference between their ages is 20 years. What will be the sum (in years) of their ages after 10 years?
questions.solution:
Ration of present ages of P and Q = 9 : 4 (given)

Let the age of P = 9x, age of Q = 4x

Difference between their ages = 20 years (given)

9x – 4x = 20

x = 20/5

x = 4

Present age of P = 9 × 4 = 36 years

Present age of Q = 4 × 4 = 16 years

Sum of their age after 10 years = 36 + 16 + (10 + 10) = 72 years.

Hence, answer is 72 years.

questions.question: A starts from a point at a speed of 30 m/s. After 3 seconds, B starts chasing A from the same point with a speed of 50 m/s. What will be the total distance (in metres) travelled by A and B before A is caught by B?
questions.solution:
Distance covered by A in 3 seconds = 30 × 3 = 90 m

Relative velocity of B w.r.t. A = (50 – 30) m/s = 20 m/s

Now, taking A to be at rest, B has to cover 90 m to catch A

⇒ Time taken by B to catch A = 90/20 = 4.5 seconds

⇒ Total distance covered by B = 4.5 × 50 = 225 m = total distance covered by A

⇒ Total distance covered by both A and B = 225 × 2 = 450 m

∴ the correct option is 2)

Putting x = y = z = n [where n is any natural number]

We get,

⇒ (7x + 3y – 5z)/5x = (7 + 3 – 5) /5 = 1

∴ the correct option is 2)

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 2 year at 20% per annum is Rs. 200. If the interest is compounded half yearly, then what is the difference (in Rs) between compound and simple interest for 1st year?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CI - SI for 2 years = P(R/100)²

⇒ 200 = P(20/100)² = P(1/5)² = P(1/25)

⇒ P = 200 × 25 = 5000 Rs.

Now,

Effective rate for SI in 1 year = 20%

Since, Interest is compounded half-yearly,

So, r = 20/2 = 10%, t = 2 cycle in 1 year

Thus,

Effective rate for CI in 2 year = 10 + 10 + (10*10)/100 = 21%

Hence, difference of interest = 21 - 20 = 1%

i.e. Difference = 1% of 5000 = 50 Rs.

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Calculation:**

⇒ CI – SI = Rs. 200

Let the principal be P

So, we have

⇒ P(1 + R/100n)ⁿt – P - (P × R × T)/100 = 200

⇒ P(1 + 20/100)² – P - (P × 20 × 2)/100 = 200

⇒ 1.44P – P – 0.4P = 200

⇒ 0.04P = 200

⇒ P = 200/0.04 = Rs. 5000

Now, the difference when compounded half yearly

⇒ [5000(1 + 20/200)² – 5000] – (5000 × 20 × 1)/100

questions.question: Due to increase of 33.33% in the price of apples, a customer can purchase 4 apples less for Rs. 16. What is the original price (in paise) of an apple?
questions.solution:
Let the price of one apple originally be ‘a’ paise

And,

Let the total number of apples be ‘b’

⇒ Total price of apples = ab

Rs 16 = 1600 paise

⇒ 1600 = ab (given) 

⇒ New price of one apple = a(1 + 33.33/100) = 1.3333a

After the increase in price,

⇒ Number of apples = b – 4

⇒ 1600 = 1.3333a × (b – 4)

⇒ 1600 = 1.3333a × [(1600/a) – 4]

⇒ 1600 = (4a/3) × [(1600 – 4a)/a]

⇒ 1200 = 1600 – 4a

⇒ 400 = 4a

⇒ a = 100

∴ the correct option is 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f72be33799c08d3322a2907949d25e7543e352bc7880a277f6efed7f62d7c04b.png]

Now price of 4 apples after increment = 16 of 33.33% 

⇒ Price of 4 apples after increment = 16 × (1/3) 

⇒ Price of one apple after increment = (16/3) × (1/4) = 4/3 

Price of one apple before increament = 4/3 × 3/4 = Rs. 1 = 100 paise 

**∴ Price of one apple before increament is 100 paise.**

options.text: The student was asked by the teacher about bringing his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he would be bringing his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.
The teacher asked the student if he has brought his lunch.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• The given question is an example of an Interrogative sentence. 
 
• 'Said to' will be changed into 'asked'. 
 
• 'If' conjunction will be added to represent whether something is true or not
 
• An interrogative statement is converted into an assertive statement. Thus, the helping verb will be placed after the subject.
 
• 'You' will be changed into 'he'. (Second person->third person)
 
• 'your' will be changed into **'his'.**
 
• 'Have' will be changed into 'had' (Present perfect tense->Past Perfect tense)

 
 
 

Therefore the correct answer is: *The teacher asked the student if he had brought his lunch.*

‘Habit’ means a regular tendency or routine. The passage emphasises on the importance of hygiene to children so that it becomes their routine. The other words do not convey the intended meaning correctly.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: susceptible

‘Susceptible’ means ‘likely to be influenced by something’. In the passage, it fits perfectly as the sentence then means that children are most likely to be harmed by skin issues, rashes, etc.

‘Avoid’ means ‘to keep away from’. The passage says that children must be taught early on what to keep away from for proper hygiene. The other words do not fit the context of hygiene and its meaning.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Select the incorrectly spelt word. **
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Sabbotage**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ‘ **Sabbotage**’ is the incorrectly spelt world. The correct spelling is ‘**sabotage**’, meaning to deliberately destroy or damage.

 
 
• Example: The disgruntled employee sought to sabotage the company's operations by intentionally deleting important files from the computer system.
 
 
 
• Let's look at the meaning of other words:
 
• **Acquiescence: **Reluctant acceptance of something without protest. 
 
 
• **Example**: After a long and contentious debate, the board members finally reached a decision through acquiescence, with some reluctantly agreeing to go along with the majority.
 
 
 
• **Alienate: **Make someone feel isolated. 
 
 
• Example: His constant criticism and harsh words began to alienate his friends, resulting in strained relationships and a sense of isolation.
 
 
 
• **Belligerent: **Hostile and aggressive. 
 
 
• Example: The drunk man became increasingly belligerent, shouting insults and picking fights with anyone who crossed his path.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.**

He shall have bought a car.

options.text: A car was being bought by him.
A car was bought by him.
A car will have been bought by him.
A car would have been bought by him.

questions.solution:
**Correct Answer**: A car will have been bought by him. 

The passive voice should use the Future Perfect Tense, as the active voice uses. This is seen only in Sentence 3, which uses ‘will have been’. The other sentences are incorrect due to their wrong tense usage.
